classification.difficultyReason: Translate labelled graph coordinates into the supplied cubic form; the hardest part requires forming and solving two simultaneous linear equations for k and c.

content.prompt: The cubic curves are in the form $y=kx^3+c$. Find its equation.

spec.description: Decreasing cubic through the origin, with a marked point (2, −4), double-arrow axes and curve ends. No grid or numbered ticks.
spec.mathematics: y=-x^3/2; marked point (2,-4); intercept (0,0). Coordinate bounds are drawing bounds, not printed axis restrictions.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve and coordinate are permanent question givens; its equation is withheld.

answer.worked:
The graph passes through the origin, so $c=0$. Using $(2,-4)$:
$$\begin{align*}-4&=k(2)^3\\-4&=8k\\k&=-\frac12\\y&=-\frac12x^3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Increasing cubic flattening at the y-axis, with y-intercept 3 and marked point (−1, 1). Double-arrow axes and curve ends; no grid or numbered ticks.
spec.mathematics: y=2x^3+3; marked point (-1,1); y-intercept 3. Coordinate bounds are drawing bounds only.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve, point and intercept label are question givens; its equation is withheld.

spec.description: Increasing cubic flattening at the y-axis below the x-axis. Marked intercepts labelled −2 and cube root of 2; double-arrow axes and curve ends, without a grid.
spec.mathematics: y=x^3-2; intercepts (0,-2) and (cube root of 2,0). Coordinate bounds are drawing bounds only.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve and both intercept labels remain question givens; its equation is withheld.

spec.description: Increasing cubic flattening at the y-axis above the x-axis, with marked points (1, 3) and (2, 10). Double-arrow axes and curve ends; no grid or numerical y-intercept label.
spec.mathematics: y=x^3+2; marked points (1,3) and (2,10). The unlabelled y-intercept remains unlabelled. Coordinate bounds are drawing bounds only.
spec.answerVisibility: Both marked coordinates and the supplied curve remain visible; the equation and derived intercept are answer content.

answer.worked:
Using $(1,3)$ and $(2,10)$:
$$\begin{align*}3&=k(1)^3+c\\3&=k+c\\10&=k(2)^3+c\\10&=8k+c\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the two equations:
$$\begin{align*}7&=7k\\k&=1\\c&=3-1\\c&=2\\y&=x^3+2\end{align*}$$
